Conclusion
Celiac disease, caused by sensitivity to dietary gluten in genetically susceptible individuals, is a disease on the rise in many parts of
the world. While the HLA-DQ genes have the strongest genetic inﬂuence on development of the disease a number of other cau-
sesdincluding non-HLA genes, infections, hygiene, and time of introduction of wheat into the diet in relation to breast fee-
dingdmay all inﬂuence expression of the disease. The disease primarily affects the small intestine, but affects many other
systems due to immune and non-immune effects. The diagnosis is made through use of serological tests followed, in most cases,
by duodenal biopsy. The disease is best treated by lifelong and complete withdrawal of wheat from the diet.
